goal.what: The developers build a product with which its users achieve their goals.

critical_success_factors.what: The developers know whom the product serves and what each of them is trying to achieve.

necessary_conditions.what: Does Roles list every kind of person who comes to the product with a goal of their own?
necessary_conditions.why: The developers build for the people Roles lists, so a missing role goes unserved, and two roles merged into one get a product that fits neither. The method is Clayton Christensen's theory of the jobs that customers hire a product for.

items.text: Define each role by the job it hires the product to do, not by a job title.
Start from the job that the product exists to do, and name who hires it for that job.
Then ask whether that job gets done only if the product also does a job for someone else, such as setting it up on a shared server. Each such person is a role as well.
Ask the user about each person whose job you can't tell from what the product does.
Split a role whose members hire the product for different jobs.
Name the role `user` where there's only one.
Read Roles as a developer would, and check that each role has a job that no other role has.

necessary_conditions.what: Does each objective state, in one sentence, what one role is trying to achieve in their own work?
necessary_conditions.why: The developers build toward the objectives, so each must name the end that a role reaches, and neither a feature nor a measure of that end. The method is the objective of John Doerr's Measure What Matters: a qualitative goal that a key result then measures.

items.text: For each role, write its job as the end they reach in their own work, in one sentence with the role as the subject.
Ask why that end matters to them until the answer is their own goal and no longer the product's.
Write one objective for each distinct end.
Read each objective with the product's name taken out, and check that it still makes sense.

necessary_conditions.what: Does the vision describe only what the users do and get, not how the product works inside?
necessary_conditions.why: The vision must stay true while the inside of the product changes, so it describes only what users do and get, and leaves how the product does it to the architecture. The method is the split between the problem space, what the users need, and the solution space, what meets the need, in Dan Olsen's The Lean Product Playbook.

items.text: For each sentence, ask whether it would change if the product's internals changed while users saw the same. If it would, move it to the architecture.

critical_success_factors.what: The developers can tell whether a change brings the users closer to their goals.

necessary_conditions.what: Does each objective have key results that measure how well and how fast its role achieves it, each with the direction that's better?
necessary_conditions.why: The developers keep a change only if it brings the users closer to their goals, so each objective needs measures that show that after a change. The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) standard 9241-11 defines usability by effectiveness and efficiency, among other measures, and these give the two key results.

items.text: Make the first key result measure how well: the share of attempts in which the role reaches the objective, or its complement, such as the share of deliverables the users can't use.
Make the second measure how fast: the time or effort the role spends to reach it.
Give each the direction that's better.
Rank them: keep a change that improves one only if none ranked before it gets worse, with how well before how fast.
Give no targets, since a measure made a target stops being a good measure, as Goodhart's law says.
Check that a developer can measure both from the records of the end-to-end (E2E) tests run after a change, and decide from them whether to keep it.

necessary_conditions.what: Are the objectives distinct, so that each piece of work serves one of them?
necessary_conditions.why: The developers decide what to build by asking which objective a piece of work serves, which works only if the objectives don't overlap. The method is Barbara Minto's rule, in The Minto Pyramid Principle, that the groups be mutually exclusive and together collectively exhaustive.

items.text: For each pair of objectives, ask whether a piece of work could serve one without the other. If not, merge them.
Take the work the product plans, and name the objective each piece serves.
A piece that serves none is either not needed or shows a missing objective. Ask the user which.

critical_success_factors.what: The developers know the one way by which the product brings its users to their goals, so that every choice leans toward it.

necessary_conditions.what: Does the concept state first the one way, as its maker means it, by which the product brings the users to their objectives, and then the ideas that keep this way holding at each moment of their use?
necessary_conditions.why: The developers make many choices that no line of the vision names, and the concept lets each of them lean the same way. Fred Brooks, in The Mythical Man-Month, calls this conceptual integrity: one set of design ideas that every part follows.

items.text: Ask the user how the product brings its users to their objectives, and by which ideas, before you write the concept, since the one way and the ideas that carry it out come from whoever conceived the product, and an analysis of what goes wrong today yields only a list of fixes with no center.
Write the one way in one sentence as what the users see the product do.
Write each idea the user gave, with what it gives the role toward the objective.

Find where the user's ideas leave the one way unheld: walk through the users' use from the moment they first meet the product to the moment they reach the objective, and list its moments, as a [customer journey map](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/journey-mapping-101/) does.
At each moment, ask what keeps the one way holding there. Where no idea answers, propose one.
Confirm each idea you propose with the user.
Drop each idea that the one way doesn't need.
Check by taking a design choice that no line names, at each of those moments, and deciding it by the one way and its ideas.
